archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A 2-2 team whose per-play profile ranks ninth in net EPA, held back by giveaways and special teams rather than by how it plays from scrimmage.

report.headline: Elite yardage margins, .500 record: turnovers and special teams are eating the Rams alive
report.take:
The Rams move the ball and stop the ball better than almost anyone. They gain 418.3 yards a game and allow 248.5, both second in the league, and they rank ninth in net EPA. The record is 2-2 with a point differential of +2 because the yards keep leaking out between the 20s and the scoreboard. They have turned it over exactly twice in all four games, sit 27th in turnover margin at -1.3 per game, and rank 30th in special-teams EPA at -4.17 per game. Those are the two most volatile parts of a football team. That gap between 2nd in yardage and 18th in scoring is the whole story.

The defense is the real engine, and it wins by a style that tends to travel: nothing over the top. It ranks first in explosive pass rate allowed and first in deep EPA allowed, third in missed-tackle rate, and seventh on third down. That is a disciplined, tackle-everything shell, and it doesn't depend on hitting the quarterback. Its pressure rate is 26th, which also helps explain why it has only three takeaways. The caveat is the schedule. Outside of San Francisco, the offenses it has faced rank 18th, 23rd and 29th in EPA today. The one elite attack it saw ran for 174 yards on it in a 27-7 loss. With Myles Garrett on IR and Aaron Donald's back limiting him, the rush is unlikely to get better soon.

Offensively this is a step back from 2025, when the Rams led the league in scoring and ranked second in offensive EPA. They are 15th now. The line is excellent in protection and in the run game: fourth in pressure allowed, second in stuff rate, third in yards per carry. Yet rush EPA is only 16th, because the yards aren't converting into value. Stafford is throwing for nearly 300 a game, but pass EPA sits at 18th, again a symptom of the turnovers. Puka Nacua has appeared in only two games, so the target tree has run through Davante Adams and Kyren Williams.

The direction is good. After the Week 1 dud, the offense has scored 24 or more three straight times and topped 300 passing yards in each. Turnover luck at -1.3 per game almost never holds over a season. A team with a top-10 net EPA and a schedule full of 1-3 and 0-4 opponents should finish well above .500.

strengths.title: A defense that erases big plays
strengths.body: The Rams allow the fewest explosive passes in the league and the lowest EPA on deep throws, backed by a top-three missed-tackle rate. That is a structural, coverage-and-tackling identity rather than a pass-rush-dependent one, so it should hold even with Garrett out. The opponents have been soft, which is the main reason to discount it a little.

strengths.title: Line controls both phases
strengths.body: Stafford has been pressured on 14.5% of dropbacks, fourth-best, and the run game rarely gets stuffed. Running backs average 3.29 yards before contact. That gives McVay a clean, on-schedule offense, which is why the yardage is elite even when the EPA isn't.

strengths.title: Per-play profile beats the record
strengths.body: A ninth-ranked net EPA with a 2-2 record and negative wins over expected says this team has played like a winning one. Last year's version was first in net EPA, so the floor of this roster is known to be high.

concerns.title: Giveaways and special teams drain points
concerns.body: Eight giveaways against three takeaways and a 30th-ranked special-teams unit explain why 418 yards a game produces just 21.3 points. The turnover side should regress toward neutral. The low takeaway count is partly real, though, because a defense that doesn't pressure doesn't force many mistakes. Special teams is the bigger unknown, since the dossier offers no cause to bet on a fix.

concerns.title: No pass rush, and it's thinner now
concerns.body: A 26th-ranked pressure rate was already the hole in this defense, and Garrett is on IR after surgery. Donald's availability is uncertain with back soreness, and starting corner Jaylen Watson is also out. Against good offenses this is where the coverage shell gets stressed. San Francisco, the only top offense faced, ran for 174 yards.

concerns.title: Penalties creeping up
concerns.body: The Rams were flagged for 91 and 100 yards in the last two games, both on the road. Combined with the giveaways, that is a lot of drives sabotaged by self-inflicted mistakes. It is likely partly noise but worth tracking.

trend.note: After a 7-point opener against San Francisco, the offense has scored 24-28 in three straight games with 300-plus passing yards each time. The defense has been steady against weaker offenses.

nextGame.headline: Stafford gets a leaky secondary; Rams D gets a real test
nextGame.body:
Buffalo is the mirror image of the Rams: a top-three offense with the league's most efficient run game, paired with a defense ranked 30th in EPA allowed. The Rams should move the ball through the air. Buffalo is 28th in pass EPA allowed and 27th in explosive passes allowed, and its tackling is 27th. The flip side is that the Bills lean run (passRateOverExp -3) and are first in rush success and yards before contact. That attacks the Rams' merely 10th-ranked run defense and a front without Garrett. Buffalo does generate pressure (8th), but the Rams' line is fourth in pressure allowed.

Availability tilts toward the Rams' passing game. Buffalo is without top corner Christian Benford, who plays 91% of snaps, and DT T.J. Sanders. Corners Dee Alford and Te'Cory Couch and DT Ed Oliver are questionable. On the Rams' side, Donald is trending toward playing per McVay, while Watson and TE Colby Parkinson are out and WR Konata Mumpfield is questionable.

keyMatchups.title: Stafford vs. depleted Bills secondary
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo is bad against the pass and missing its starting corner, with two more corners questionable. The Rams' line has kept Stafford clean. This is the spot for the passing game's yardage to finally turn into points.

keyMatchups.title: Bills run game vs. Rams front
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo leads the league in rush success and yards before contact. The Rams are 10th against the run and lost Garrett. If Buffalo stays on schedule on the ground, the Rams' deep-coverage strength matters less.

keyMatchups.title: Ball security decides it
keyMatchups.body: The Rams have given it away twice in every game. Against an offense scoring 31.8 a game, short fields could flip a game the Rams should control on a per-play basis.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Rams finally play a clean game: zero or one giveaway likely means a comfortable home win.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the record to catch up with the play. The per-play numbers are strong and the turnover margin is an outlier that should regress. The middle of the schedule is soft: Arizona twice, the Chargers, Washington and Green Bay, all with losing or .500 records. The defense's numbers will likely slip some once it faces more offenses like Kansas City, San Francisco and Dallas late, and the pass rush is a real limitation until Garrett returns.

The ceiling depends on the offense getting back toward its 2025 efficiency. The line play and the passing yardage suggest it is closer than 15th in EPA implies. The division is the problem: San Francisco and Seattle are a combined 7-1 and the Rams play them three more times, so a wild-card path looks more realistic than the division right now.

bets.reason: The Rams have the better net EPA (0.104 vs 0.078) and play at home. Buffalo is 75% ATS with positive wins over expected while the Rams' turnover luck has been among the worst in the league. Buffalo's corner injuries hit exactly where Stafford can attack.

Buffalo ranks 28th in pass EPA allowed and 27th in explosive passes allowed and is without its 91%-snap corner. The Rams' line has allowed pressure at the fourth-lowest rate, so Buffalo's 8th-ranked rush is less of a threat.

confidence.note: Four games, soft opponents for the defense, and a thinned pass rush.
